fidelity: F2a — Physics-Lumped Ideal Cycle (Schmidt isothermal) + Warm-up ODE
source: Urieli & Berchowitz (1984) Stirling Cycle Engine Analysis, Adam Hilger; Walker (1980) Stirling Engines, Oxford University Press; Schmidt (1871).

engine.name: Generic kinematic alpha-type Stirling engine (micro-CHP scale, ~9 kW class, e.g. WhisperGen / GPU-3 family)
engine.note: Reuses F1a device class (P_rated, T_h, T_c, f_carnot) and adds first-principles Schmidt geometry.

f_carnot.note: Fraction-of-Carnot proxy carried from F1a (cross-check only)

V_swept_exp.note: Expansion-space swept volume (120 cm^3 per cycle)

phase_deg.note: Phase angle between expansion and compression pistons (alpha)

dead_volume_ratio.note: Total dead volume / total swept volume (regenerator+heater+cooler+clearance)

mech_eff.note: Mechanical efficiency (friction, windage) applied to indicated power

pumping_coeff.note: Pumping/flow-loss fraction of indicated power (gas circuit dP)

gas_properties.note: Ideal-gas specific gas constant R = R_univ/M; cited at 300-900 K mean. Source: NIST / Lemmon et al.; Walker (1980) Table for Stirling working fluids.

hydrogen.note: Diatomic; best Stirling fluid by power density

thermal.note: Lumped heater-head warm-up: C_th dT_h/dt = Q_burner - Q_to_gas - Q_loss.

Q_burner.note: Burner heat delivered to head at full fire
